items.name: Task format
items.desc:
The format that Tasks uses to read and write tasks.

Important: Tasks currently only supports one format at a time. Selecting Dataview will currently stop Tasks reading its own emoji signifiers.

items.name: Global filter
items.desc:
Recommended: Leave empty if you want all checklist items in your vault to be tasks managed by this plugin.

Use a global filter if you want Tasks to only act on a subset of your "- [ ]" checklist items, so that a checklist item must include the specified string in its description in order to be considered a task.

For example, if you set the global filter to #task, the Tasks plugin will only handle checklist items tagged with #task. Other checklist items will remain normal checklist items and not appear in queries or get a done date set.

items.name: Remove global filter from description
items.desc: Enabling this removes the string that you set as global filter from the task description when displaying a task.

items.name: Task statuses
items.desc:
Core statuses

These are the core statuses that Tasks supports natively, with no need for custom CSS styling or theming.

Custom statuses

You can add and edit your own custom statuses in the Custom statuses section.

You should first select and install a CSS snippet or theme to style custom checkboxes. Then, set up your custom statuses to match your chosen CSS checkboxes.

See the documentation to get started!

modal.title: Core statuses
modal.html:
These are the core statuses that Tasks supports natively, with no need for custom CSS styling or theming.

You can add and edit your own custom statuses in the Custom statuses section.

items.name: Review and check your statuses
items.desc: Create a new file in the root of the vault, containing a Mermaid diagram of the current status settings.

modal.title: Custom statuses
modal.html:
You should first select and install a CSS snippet or theme to style custom checkboxes.

Then, set up your custom statuses to match your chosen CSS checkboxes.

Note Any statuses with the same symbol as any earlier statuses will be ignored. You can confirm the actually loaded statuses by running the 'Create or edit task' command and looking at the Status drop-down.

items.name: Import from theme
items.desc: Add the statuses supported by a theme or CSS snippet.

items.name: Add all unknown status types
items.desc: Add any status symbols found in your vault but not yet configured here.

items.name: Reset custom status types to defaults
items.desc: Discard all custom statuses and restore the defaults.

items.name: Presets
items.desc:
You can define named instructions here, that you can re-use in multiple queries. A preset called 'name' can be used in Tasks queries with either 'preset name' or '{{preset.name}}'.

Any open Tasks queries are reloaded automatically when presets are edited.

See the documentation.

items.name: this_file
items.desc: path includes {{query.file.path}}

items.name: this_folder
items.desc: folder includes {{query.file.folder}}

items.name: this_folder_only
items.desc: filter by function task.file.folder === query.file.folder

items.name: this_root
items.desc: root includes {{query.file.root}}

items.name: Global query
items.desc: Instructions automatically included at the start of every Tasks block.

items.name: Enable custom searches
items.desc: Enables 'filter by function', 'sort by function', and 'group by function', which execute JavaScript in Tasks queries.

items.name: Task count location
items.desc: Choose whether the task count is shown at the top or bottom of query results.

items.name: Set created date on every added task
items.desc: Enabling this will add a timestamp ➕ YYYY-MM-DD before other date values, when a task is created with 'Create or edit task', or by completing a recurring task.

items.name: Set done date on every completed task
items.desc: Enabling this will add a timestamp ✅ YYYY-MM-DD at the end when a task is toggled to done.

items.name: Set cancelled date on every cancelled task
items.desc: Enabling this will add a timestamp ❌ YYYY-MM-DD at the end when a task is toggled to cancelled.

items.name: Use filename as Scheduled date for undated tasks
items.desc:
Save time entering Scheduled (⏳) dates. If this option is enabled, any undated tasks will be given a default Scheduled date extracted from their file name.

By default, Tasks plugin will match both YYYY-MM-DD and YYYYMMDD date formats. Undated tasks have none of Due (📅 ), Scheduled (⏳) and Start (🛫) dates.

items.name: Additional filename date format as Scheduled date for undated tasks
items.desc: An additional date format that Tasks plugin will recogize when using the file name as the Scheduled date for undated tasks.

items.name: Folders with default Scheduled dates
items.desc: Leave empty if you want to use default Scheduled dates everywhere, or enter a comma-separated list of folders.

items.name: Next recurrence appears on the line below
items.desc: Enabling this will make the next recurrence of a task appear on the line below the completed task. Otherwise the next recurrence will appear before the completed one.

items.name: Remove scheduled date on recurrence
items.desc:
Enabling this will make the next recurrence of a task have no Scheduled (⏳) date, when at least one of Start (🛫) or Due (📅) dates is present.

This is for when you want the Start and Due dates to carry forward to the next recurrence, but you will set the Scheduled date in future, once you plan to work on it.

items.name: Auto-suggest task content
items.desc: Enabling this will open an intelligent suggest menu while typing inside a recognized task line.

items.name: Minimum match length for auto-suggest
items.desc: If higher than 0, auto-suggest will be triggered only when the beginning of any supported keywords is recognized.

items.name: Maximum number of auto-suggestions to show
items.desc: How many suggestions should be shown when an auto-suggest menu pops up (including the "⏎" option).

items.name: Provide access keys in dialogs
items.desc: If the access keys (keyboard shortcuts) for various controls in dialog boxes conflict with system keyboard shortcuts or assistive technology functionality that is important for you, you may want to deactivate them here.
